nodes.label: The system shall create an inventory item from a request carrying a client-supplied SKU, name, description, and initial quantity.

why.q: Item data model: what fields define an inventory item?
why.a: B. Minimal + description - SKU, name, description, quantity. (Simplest shape that still supports useful CRUD for a very simple API; price/category/reorder metadata deferred.)

why.q: SKU ownership: who assigns the item's unique identifier?
why.a: A. Client-supplied SKU is the unique identifier; the API rejects duplicates on create. (Keeps the model simple - one identifier, no separate generated id.)

why.a: A. Hard delete - the item record is removed and subsequent reads return not-found. (Simplest delete semantics; soft-delete/archival and movement history are explicitly out of scope.)

why.q: Stock adjustment semantics: how do callers change quantity?
why.a: A. Relative delta only - callers send a signed delta (+/-) applied atomically; no direct absolute-set path. (Matches the concurrency-safe adjustment Must and keeps the surface minimal.)

nodes.label: Create an item
nodes.text: As Alex the Integrating Developer, I want to create an inventory item with a SKU, name, description, and initial quantity, so that it exists as a programmatic record I can read and adjust.

nodes.label: Get an item by SKU
nodes.text: As Alex, I want to retrieve a single item by its SKU, so that my application can read its current data.

nodes.label: List items with pagination
nodes.text: As Alex, I want to list items in bounded pages, so that I can enumerate inventory without unbounded responses.

nodes.label: Update an item's descriptive fields
nodes.text: As Alex, I want to update an item's name and description by SKU, so that item metadata stays correct.

nodes.label: Delete an item
nodes.text: As Alex, I want to hard-delete an item by SKU, so that obsolete items are removed.

nodes.label: Adjust stock by a relative delta
nodes.text: As Alex, I want to adjust an item's quantity by a signed delta, so that stock levels stay accurate as goods move.

nodes.label: Concurrent adjustments do not lose updates
nodes.text: As Alex, I want concurrent adjustments to the same item to be applied atomically, so that no update is silently lost under load.

nodes.label: Consistent, machine-readable errors
nodes.text: As Alex, I want every failure to return one consistent error shape, so that my application can handle errors programmatically.

nodes.label: Input validation at the boundary
nodes.text: As Alex, I want all inputs validated at the API boundary, so that malformed data never reaches the datastore and I get a clear error.

nodes.label: Health check and structured logging
nodes.text: As Sam the Operator, I want a health-check endpoint and structured request logs, so that I can gate deploys and diagnose issues.
